regime_context: US thematic leadership is concentrated at the top in the semiconductor complex (Memory/HBM, AI Infrastructure, WFE) with eligible breadth narrowing (21/49, frac 0.43) and absorption at 0.31. The absolute-trend gate is validated as risk control on this market's history (gate_helps true), but relative momentum rank is an attention lens (rank-IC ~0) and rotation timing has no forward edge, so any lean is a fallible durability judgement, not a prediction.
emerging_watch: Watching whether the one-narrative structure forms: absorption is low (0.31) and one_narrative is false, but if Memory/HBM's margin over AI Infrastructure widens past ~0.8 while eligible breadth keeps narrowing below 0.35, that would mark a genuine single-theme regime. I retire this watch if the margin falls back below 0.3 and two or more challengers (AI Infra, Semis WFE, Cybersecurity) hold top-3 ranks through the next two weeks.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity screens as the most extended eligible theme: crowded flag true (crowding_z 1.91, the highest of any eligible theme) with perfect breadth 1.0 and trend-tagged durability. While crowd flags are a size-down caution only and never a fade, the combination of peak crowding with full breadth and a top-4 momentum rank suggests the risk-reward for adding here is poor. This is expressed as an underweight rather than a short, per guardrails.
evidence: crowded: true, crowding_z 1.91 (highest among eligible themes)
theses.dissent: Trend persistence in security software can outlast crowding flags for many months; crowding is a coincident texture with no basket-level forward edge, and a full-breadth uptrend has historically been the most robust regime to stay in.

falsifier.text: CIBR makes a new 20-day relative high versus SPY while breadth holds at 1.0 and crowding_z stays below 2.0 through the check-by date

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Memory/HBM is the confirmed leader (rank 1, score 2.59) with solid breadth 0.75 and crowded false, meaning it is NOT yet in the extended/attention-peak regime the guardrails warn about. The absolute-trend gate confirms eligibility, which is the one validated risk-control leg. The lean is modest because rotation timing has no forward edge and the lead is mid-sized (margin 0.458 over AI Infra).
evidence: rank 1, score 2.59, eligible true (absolute-trend gate passed)
theses.dissent: Memory is a deeply cyclical sub-sector with mean-reverting earnings; the 'mixed' hurst_tag (not clean trend) and a margin of only 0.458 over AI Infrastructure suggests leadership could rotate without warning, and rank-IC ~0 means the #1 rank carries no alpha signal.

falsifier.text: SMH-relative Memory names (the HBM/storage cohort) lag AI Infrastructure by more than 3% while memory's eligibility gate flips false before the check-by date

theses.subject: AI Infrastructure
theses.thesis: AI Infrastructure is the closest challenger (rank 2, score 2.132) with the highest breadth among semiconductors (0.875) and crowded false, so it is not in the attention-peak zone. It shares the SMH proxy with Memory/WFE, so this is a modest tilt within the same complex rather than an independent call. The absolute-trend gate is passed.
theses.dissent: Same ETF proxy (SMH) as three other top-5 themes means this 'theme' is not cleanly separable from Memory and WFE; heavy overlap means any lean is effectively one bet on the semiconductor complex, and the AI capex narrative has a crowded-capex counter-risk not visible in this snapshot.

falsifier.text: AI Infrastructure cohort underperforms the broad semiconductor complex by 2% while its breadth drops below 0.7 before the check-by date
